entries.title: Magic balance
changes: Ember, Frost Bolt and Magic Missile are no longer free. Each cast costs half a hunger point, and they recharge in 2 to 2.5 seconds instead of 1 to 1.5, so they stay handy without replacing a bow.
Polymorph no longer works on villagers, wandering traders, tamed animals or anything with a name tag.
Tunnel recharges in 15 seconds instead of 5 and costs 3 hunger instead of 2.
Goodberry takes 2 bone meal instead of 1.

entries.title: The Magic Update: cauldrons, cooking and spells
changes: Potions are now brewed in the cauldron. Pour in Bottles of Mystical Essence, add the ingredients in order, stir with the new Iron Ladle and keep a fire, campfire, lava or magma block underneath. Every vanilla potion has a new recipe. Gunpowder added last makes a splash potion, then dragon's breath a lingering one, so tipped arrows work again.
The brewing stand now makes one thing: Bottles of Mystical Essence, from water, Diamond Dust and nether wart. One diamond crafts into 4 Diamond Dust.
Standing in a cauldron of finished potion gives you its effect, and drains the cauldron as you do. Mobs too, so a cauldron of harming makes a trap.

The cauldron is also a cooking pot. Put food into water, milk or honey, stir it over heat and scoop out bowls of soup. There are ten new soups, including Golden Carrot Soup and a Nether Stew that needs lava underneath, and the vanilla stews come out better from a cauldron. Add any food as an extra, or pour a potion in to season it (weaker, shared between the bowls). Each bowl is coloured by what went into it.
New crop: garlic. Break an allium and you may find a bulb.

Dairy: cows and mooshrooms sometimes drop rennet. Churn cold milk in a cauldron into butter, or heat milk with rennet into a cheese wheel that ages from fresh to aged over a few days. Slice it by hand or craft a wheel into 9 slices. Garlic bread is bread, garlic and butter.

The Potion Book lists every soup, and every potion you've learned, with exactly how to make it. Learn potions from Knowledge Scrolls found in villages, dungeons and trial chambers, or by working a recipe out yourself. The new do_global_knowledge game rule lets everyone share what anyone learns.

Spells: 46 of them across eight schools, from Fire, Frost and Storm to Life, Death and Nature. Each is learned from a spell tome sold by the new Arcanist villager (who works at an enchanting table) or found in one particular structure.

Cast with a wand, which uses spells you've learned while their tome is in your inventory, or a staff, which holds tomes in its own slots. Staffs range from the 1-slot Wooden Staff to the 25-slot Legendary Staff, found only in ancient cities. Right-click casts, sneak and scroll picks a spell, and the Open Staff key (R) opens a staff's slots.
Magic has no mana bar. Spells cost hunger, experience, reagents or diamond dust, and all have cooldowns.
One spell has no tome to find: shear an allay while it holds soul sand to learn Summon Vexes.

entries.title: Added obsidian chests
changes: New obsidian chest: 54 slots, 108 as a double, and locked to whoever placed it. Its owner gets an Access button on the chest's window to choose who else can open it and what a comparator reads. Hoppers can fill it but not empty it, and a comparator reads a pulse on each authorised opening or each refused attempt instead of its contents.
Chests with more than six rows now scroll, with a scroll bar like the creative inventory's.
Obsidian chests are in the Functional Blocks and Redstone Blocks creative tabs.
Placing two obsidian chests side by side now joins them into one 108-slot double chest, instead of leaving two separate inventories that could not be opened.
Double chests no longer show a line down the middle. Any chest that only has a single-chest texture, modded ones included, now joins seamlessly into a double.

entries.title: Permissions for every command
changes: Every command, the game's own and every mod's, now has a permission node, such as minecraft.command.gamemode or mymod.command.home. With nothing set up, commands work exactly as they did before.
Permission groups come from datapacks, in data/<namespace>/permission_group/. Groups can inherit from each other, apply to everyone or to an op level, and use wildcards and denials.
The new /permissions command (or /perms) shows what anyone may do and why, puts players in groups, and allows or denies single commands for one player.
On singleplayer and LAN worlds, /op and /deop now work, so the host can give friends commands without turning them on for everyone. The host always has every permission while commands are on.
The game window now really does show the ABNW icon.
Villagers can walk through doorways with a carpet laid in them. They are a hair shorter to fit, which nobody will notice.

entries.title: ABNW by name
changes: The game window is now titled ABNW with its version, and it uses the ABNW icon, the same one as the launcher.
Mods can now give extra attributes to any mob, including the game's own.

entries.title: Light that answers, and light you can build with
changes: Redstone lamps and copper bulbs light the world again when they turn on, instead of only changing how they look. The same was true of furnaces, smokers and blast furnaces while lit, of redstone ore, of candles, of respawn anchors, sea pickles, cave vines, light blocks, trial spawners and vaults, and all of them now give the light they should.
A campfire, a redstone torch and a light block no longer give off light when they are out or dimmed.
New slabs and stairs for glass, all 16 stained glasses and tinted glass. They stay as clear as the glass they are cut from and, like glass, need silk touch to come back.
New glowstone and shroomlight slabs and stairs, and redstone lamp and copper bulb slabs and stairs that still answer redstone and light up as the whole block does.
New copper grate slabs and stairs, at every stage of copper and in waxed and bare forms.

Bare copper cuts weather where they stand, just as the whole blocks do: a copper bulb or grate slab goes from copper to exposed, weathered and oxidized. Honeycomb holds one at the stage it has reached, and an axe scrapes the wax off or takes it back a stage.
Vertical slabs are now placed by sneaking, the way vertical stairs are. Placed without sneaking, a slab lands exactly where it always did, so the top half is reachable on every face again.

entries.title: Doors keep their carpet in the right half
changes: A carpet laid into a door stays in the bottom half. The top half no longer copies it, and opening or powering the door no longer takes the bottom half's carpet away.
The upper half of a sunflower, lilac, peony, rose bush or large fern cannot be carpeted either: a carpet lies in the half that meets the floor.

entries.title: Carpetlogging, a new title screen, and mods that share
changes: Carpets can be laid into a block's own space, the way water fills one: put a carpet under a chest, a slab, a fence or anything else that leaves room and it stays there with the block.
Wool, moss and pale moss carpets can all be laid this way. Shears lift the carpet back off, and breaking the block drops both.
The title screen now wears ABNW's own logo.

Two mods that reach for the same behaviour no longer cancel each other out: targeting, damage, drops, riding, fluid flow, loot, the camera and model poses all gather what every mod has to say before deciding.

entries.title: Vertical slabs and stairs, and new building blocks
changes: Slabs can be placed vertically: click the side of a block and the slab goes against it, facing the way you look.
Sneak while placing stairs to stand them vertically. Vertical and ordinary stairs join into corners in every direction.
New slabs and stairs for all 16 colours of wool and concrete. Concrete ones can also be made in the stonecutter.
New dirt and grass slabs. Grass slabs spread like grass, and grass spreads onto dirt slabs.
Wool slabs and stairs burn, dampen vibrations and are quick to shear, like wool.
Players joining a world over Steam now receive the terrain below the surface as the host does.

entries.title: Faster cubic rendering and wider worlds
changes: Large render distances are smooth again thanks to cubic chunk cache and rebuild optimisations.
Worlds now reach close to the 32-bit coordinate limit horizontally.
Sound stays precise far from spawn.

entries.title: A Brand New World
changes: The first ABNW release.
